question_bank.stem: At test time, how does the trained diffusion model generate an image from noise?

options.text: It starts from an initialization and repeatedly predicts and subtracts noise.
It starts from a clean image and repeatedly adds noise for training labels.
It starts from a discriminator and repeatedly labels samples as real.
It starts from a trigger patch and repeatedly changes the training set.

question_bank.explanation: Sampling reverses training-time noising by repeatedly denoising from an initial noisy image until structure appears.

distractor_rationales.B: Describes the forward training process rather than test-time sampling.
distractor_rationales.C: Describes GAN discrimination rather than diffusion sampling.
distractor_rationales.D: Describes data poisoning rather than generation.

source_ref.evidence_span: You are going to perform a progressive denoising.

frame_evidence.description: Sampling slide shows an initialization passed through repeated diffusion-model calls.

question_bank.stem: A user wants a dog instead of whatever image vanilla sampling produces. What addition addresses that need?

options.text: Condition the model on a prompt or another modality during generation.
Remove all prompts so the model can follow the random image alone.
Replace denoising with a discriminator trained on real and fake labels.
Insert a hidden trigger into the training data before deployment.

question_bank.explanation: The instructor answers that vanilla generation goes where the model goes; practical systems use conditioning such as text prompts.

distractor_rationales.B: Removing prompts does not guide generation toward a requested object.
distractor_rationales.C: This switches to a GAN-like setup rather than conditioned diffusion.
distractor_rationales.D: This is a backdoor mechanism rather than normal prompt conditioning.

frame_evidence.description: Sampling slide is followed by discussion of prompt-conditioned generation.

question_bank.stem: Why does latent diffusion run noising and denoising in z space instead of pixel space?

options.text: The latent space is lower-dimensional while retaining important image patterns.
The latent space is higher-dimensional while removing all image structure.
The latent space is a discriminator label space for real and fake samples.
The latent space is a prompt string space for direct instruction attacks.

question_bank.explanation: Latent diffusion uses an encoder to compress images into a manageable representation, performs diffusion there, and decodes back to pixels.

distractor_rationales.B: Reverses the compression purpose and loses the needed representation.
distractor_rationales.C: Confuses latent diffusion with GAN discrimination.
distractor_rationales.D: Confuses latent vectors with prompt-injection strings.

source_ref.evidence_span: You use an encoder to encode it in a lower-dimensional space.

frame_evidence.description: Latent diffusion slide shows x mapped to z, denoising in latent space, then decoding back.
